items.title: Reflexivity of a coherent module on an integral normal scheme is torsion freeness plus S2, equivalently extendability from a big open
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives three equivalent descriptions of reflexivity for a coherent module on an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme: reflexivity, torsion freeness together with property S2, and being the pushforward of a finite locally free restriction from an open whose complement has codimension at least two (statement lines 2254-2270). The counted proof is a genuine three-way organisation: it reduces the first equivalence to normal local rings by the affine criterion, derives the easy implication from the extension lemma and the depth of points outside a big open, and then constructs the big open as the maximal locus where the module is finite locally free, proving that its complement has local dimension at least two using that local rings of dimension at most one are fields or discrete valuation rings, and that the module extends across it because of depth at least two (proof lines 2272-2301). It is H2: the argument is complete in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard criteria and the extension lemma.
